name: refyntra
description: A free code companion for writing, analysing and navigating code: find anything, see how code is connected (callers, implementations, tests, request handlers, endpoints, DI registrations), get focused diagnostics and rename safely with a preview. C# is analysed with Roslyn; TypeScript and JavaScript use VS Code's built-in language features; Python and Rust use the Pyright and rust-analyzer language servers bundled with Refyntra, so no other extension is needed.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode Refyntra only lists solution and project files and shows its UI and health. It does not start the C# host, does not run MSBuild evaluation, restore, build, source generators or analyzers, and does not read the refyntra.hostPath setting from the workspace, and does not start the bundled Python (Pyright) or Rust (rust-analyzer) language servers. Find, Related, Actions and Rename explain that the workspace must be trusted.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Refyntra needs a local file system and a local .NET host.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Paste a stack trace to open its frames in your code: .NET (including async, lambdas, Mono and Unity), JavaScript/TypeScript, Python and Rust. Files are matched by path; .NET frames without a usable file are looked up by symbol. Nothing is run.
[Open Stack Trace](command:refyntra.openStackTrace)

Refyntra helps you write, analyse and navigate code: find anything, see how code is connected (callers, implementations, tests, request handlers, endpoints, DI registrations), get focused diagnostics and rename safely with a preview.
To start, open a C# file and put the cursor on a class, interface or method, then choose Related. TypeScript and JavaScript files work too.
[Related](command:refyntra.related)
[Find](command:refyntra.find)
[Actions](command:refyntra.actions)
[Rename](command:refyntra.rename)
[Health](command:refyntra.showHealth)
[Keyboard shortcuts](command:refyntra.keyboardShortcuts)
[Get started](command:refyntra.getStarted)

This workspace is in Restricted Mode. Refyntra does not start its C# backend (no MSBuild, restore or build) until you trust the workspace, so Find, Related, Actions and Rename are unavailable for C#.
[Manage Workspace Trust](command:workbench.trust.manage)
[Health](command:refyntra.showHealth)
[Get started](command:refyntra.getStarted)

No C# solution or project was found in this workspace. Open a folder with a .sln, .slnx or .csproj file, or choose one. TypeScript and JavaScript files still work: put the cursor on a symbol and choose Related.
[Select Solution](command:refyntra.selectSolution)
[Related](command:refyntra.related)
[Find](command:refyntra.find)
[Get started](command:refyntra.getStarted)

The Refyntra C# backend could not start, so C# features are unavailable. The Health page shows the reason and how to fix it (for example a missing .NET SDK).
[Health](command:refyntra.showHealth)
[Restart Backend](command:refyntra.restartBackend)
[Export Debug Bundle](command:refyntra.exportDebugBundle)
[Get started](command:refyntra.getStarted)

Collect the symbols, files, endpoints and relations you work on for a task. Items are stored locally for this workspace and found again after code changes (resolved, moved, ambiguous or missing).
[New Task Context](command:refyntra.taskContext.new)
[Add Symbol at Cursor](command:refyntra.taskContext.addSymbol)

Refyntra runs and debugs .NET projects (console, web, worker; Windows Forms and WPF on Windows), package.json scripts, Python files and Cargo binaries without other extensions. Open a folder with a solution or project; runnable projects appear here once it has loaded.
[Select What to Run](command:refyntra.selectRunTarget)
[Generate launch.json](command:refyntra.generateLaunchJson)
[Health](command:refyntra.showHealth)

Restricted Mode: building and running execute code from this workspace, so Refyntra does not run or debug anything until you trust it.

refyntra.hostPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to `Refyntra.Host.dll` (started with `dotnet`) or to a host executable. Empty = the host bundled with the extension. Machine scope only: a workspace cannot change which executable runs.

refyntra.rename.apply.markdownDescription: Offer **Apply rename** after the preview. After you confirm, the plan is revalidated, every target file is checked against the previewed text, the edit is applied to the editor buffers (not saved) and the result is reconciled per file. Undo works through the editor. Turn off for preview-only renames.

enumDescriptions: No Refyntra keybindings. F12, Shift+F12 and your shortcuts stay untouched.
Visual Studio-like (default): Ctrl+, Find, Ctrl+. Actions, Ctrl+R Ctrl+R Rename, Ctrl+Shift+Alt+F12 Related.
ReSharper-like: Ctrl+T Find, Alt+Enter Actions, Ctrl+Shift+R Rename, Ctrl+Shift+G Related.
refyntra.keybindings.preset.markdownDescription: Keybinding preset for Find / Related / Actions / Rename. Presets override some VS Code defaults (e.g. Ctrl+T, Ctrl+.) while active; choose `none` to turn Refyntra shortcuts off.

refyntra.postfix.enabled.markdownDescription: Offer C# postfix templates after a dot (`items.foreach`, `flag.if`, `value.var`, `task.await`…). The C# host chooses the templates from the expression's type; they are listed after the regular members.

refyntra.http.basePaths.markdownDescription: Frontend ↔ backend links (heuristic): path prefixes that client calls add but the ASP.NET routes do not have (for example `/backend` when a dev proxy removes it). By default only exact route matches are linked; a prefix is removed from the client URL only when the exact match finds nothing.

refyntra.http.origins.markdownDescription: Frontend ↔ backend links (heuristic): absolute origins that are this backend, for example `https://localhost:5001`. Client calls to any other absolute URL are never linked.

refyntra.related.followCursor.description: Update the Related view when the cursor moves (unless the view is pinned).

refyntra.trace.level.description: Log level of the Refyntra output channel. Logs never contain source text.

refyntra.cleanup.profile.markdownDescription: Fixes pre-selected by **Refyntra: Code Cleanup** (each run can toggle them). Every fix is applied only where Roslyn proves the code means the same; anything else is skipped with the reason in the preview. `fileScopedNamespace` and `whitespace` act only when `.editorconfig` asks for them (`csharp_style_namespace_declarations = file_scoped`, `trim_trailing_whitespace`, `insert_final_newline`). Files are never saved automatically.

refyntra.rules.OR1001.markdownDescription: Experimental rule OR1001 "scoped service captured by a singleton": reported only for a proven constructor path inside one composition root ([docs](https://github.com/refyntra/refyntra/blob/main/docs/rules/OR1001.md)). When it cannot prove a path it stays silent; the reason is shown by the code action *Refyntra: why OR1001 did not check this registration*, never in Problems.

enumDescriptions: Show text-only plans in the editor's Refactor Preview panel (grouped per file; apply or discard there). Refyntra revalidates before showing it and checks every file again before handing the edit over; plans that create, rename or delete files use the QuickPick preview.
Show every plan as a summary document with a QuickPick of per-file diffs and an Apply item (one list, fully keyboard and screen-reader operable).
refyntra.preview.style.description: Where Refyntra shows a refactoring preview before anything is applied.

enumDescriptions: A dialog with the parameter table (drag or Alt+Up/Down to reorder, live signature preview).
QuickPick steps (one parameter at a time).
refyntra.changeSignature.editor.description: How Change Signature edits the parameter list.

refyntra.codeLens.enabled.description: Show CodeLens above C# types and methods (references, implementations, tests, MediatR, endpoints, EF Core). Resolved lazily only for visible lines.

refyntra.codeLens.references.description: CodeLens: "N references · N implementations · N tests".

refyntra.codeLens.mediatr.description: CodeLens: MediatR "→ Handler: X" on requests and "← sent from N places" on handlers.

refyntra.codeLens.endpoints.description: CodeLens: ASP.NET Core endpoints ("GET /api/... · N frontend calls").

refyntra.codeLens.efCore.description: CodeLens: EF Core "→ configuration · N migrations".

refyntra.hover.mediatr.description: Hover on a MediatR request shows its handler with a link.

refyntra.run.codeLens.markdownDescription: Show **Run | Debug** above `Main`/top-level `Program.cs`, Python `if __name__ == "__main__":` and Rust `fn main()`.

refyntra.run.statusBar.markdownDescription: Show the run target picker (project · profile · framework) in the status bar.

refyntra.run.editorButtons.markdownDescription: Show **Run** and **Debug** buttons in the editor title of C#, Python and Rust files.

refyntra.run.view.markdownDescription: Show the **Refyntra Run** view (runnable projects with Run, Debug and Stop) in the Refyntra side bar.

refyntra.debug.inlineValues.markdownDescription: Show values of C# locals, parameters and assigned fields after the lines of the stopped method (up to the stopped line) while debugging with `refyntra-dotnet`. Only names and `this.member` are evaluated (watch context), never method calls; netcoredbg may run property getters. VS Code shows them when `#debug.inlineValues#` is `auto` (the default, which uses language providers like this one) or `on`.

project.description: The .csproj to build before launching (dotnet build). Leave out to start "program" as is.

framework.description: Target framework to build and run (multi-targeting projects), e.g. net10.0.

launchProfile.description: The launchSettings.json profile the configuration was generated from (informational).

program.description: The built .dll (started with dotnet) or apphost to debug.

console.description: netcoredbg starts the program itself and writes its output to the Debug Console; the terminal values are accepted, but output still goes to the Debug Console (use Run for a terminal).

justMyCode.description: Step and break only in user code.

launchBrowser.description: Web apps: open the browser when the app writes "Now listening on".

python.description: Interpreter (default: python.defaultInterpreterPath, .venv/venv, or python on PATH).
